extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: A multimodal 3D medical imaging dataset pairing 50,188 reconstructed 3D chest CT volumes (over 14.3 million 2D slices) from 25,692 non-contrast scans across 21,304 unique patients with corresponding radiology text reports, annotated for 18 distinct abnormalities, organ-level anatomical segmentation, and accompanied by a visual question-answering (VQA) dataset.
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Chenyu Wang, Furkan Almas, Ayse Gulnihan Simsek, Sewal Nil Esirgun, Irem Dogan, Omer Faruk Durugol, Benjamin Hou, Suprosanna Shit, Weicheng Dai, Murong Xu, Hadrien Reynaud, Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen, Bastian Wittmann, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Enis Simsar, Mehmet Simsar, Emine Bensu Erdemir, Abdullah Alanbay, Anjany Sekuboyina, Berkan Lafci, Ahmet Kaplan, Zhiyong Lu, Malgorzata Polacin, Bemhard Kainz, Christian Bluethgen, Kayhan Batmanghelich, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir, Bjoem Menze
extraction.citeAs: Hamamci, I. E., et al. (2025). Developing generalist foundation models from a multimodal dataset for 3D computed tomography. arXiv:2403.17834v4.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes and corresponding free-text radiology reports were collected from the hospital database of Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, incorporating every reconstructed volume across different reconstruction kernels to accommodate diverse window settings.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast 3D chest CT scans and associated radiology reports acquired from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital using Philips, Siemens, and PNMS (Philips-Neusoft Medical Systems) CT scanners.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized using targeted searches with regular expressions to remove date-related details and patient-doctor identifiers. Anonymized reports were translated from Turkish to English via the Google Translate API and subsequently reviewed, corrected, and cleared of residual personal data by bilingual final-year medical students. CT volumes with contrast material or covering non-chest body regions were excluded. Metadata was anonymized by removing all patient and clinician identifying information, and scan orientation was standardized.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Volumes were resized to achieve uniform voxel spacing of 0.75 mm in the x- and y-axes and 1.5 mm in the z-axis, then center-cropped or padded to a uniform resolution of 480×480×240. Voxel intensities were converted to Hounsfield Units (HU) using intercept and slope values from metadata, clipped to the range [-1000, 1000], and normalized to [-1, 1] during training.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 1,000 reports were manually annotated by combining findings and impression sections to label 18 distinct abnormalities (conditions not referenced were deemed absent). This annotated subset was split into 800 training and 200 validation reports to fine-tune RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, which was subsequently deployed to automatically label the remaining 24,692 reports. Additionally, organ-level anatomical segmentation masks were generated using a CADS model, pulmonary nodule metadata was generated via TotalSegmentator, and a VQA dataset of over 2.7 million QA pairs was generated using Llama 3.1 8B and rule-based extraction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Conditions not referenced in either the findings or impression sections were treated as absent. Related findings were grouped together: left and right mucoid impactions under mucoid impaction; lung opacity, density increase, and ground-glass opacities under lung opacity; and lung and fissural nodules under lung nodules.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students (for translation verification, report anonymization, and manual report annotation).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, Google Translate API, Meta Llama 3.1 8B, TotalSegmentator
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to extend CT-RATE with multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels for 3D chest CT volumes as part of future work; anatomical segmentation labels are released via the CT-RATE Hugging Face repository.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient age (ranging from 18 to 102 years) and patient sex (41.6% female, 58.4% male). Personal identifiers and date-related information were purged.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to address the acute shortage of open-source 3D medical imaging datasets with text reports, alleviate radiologist workloads, reduce diagnostic errors, and assist in situations where immediate radiological expertise is unavailable.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The primary dataset originates from a single hospital center and geographic setting, which introduces single-institution biases and may limit the generalizability of models across broader populations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Single-center geographic and clinical scope; reliance on specific report terminology and prompt phrasing during zero-shot detection; performance still falls short of thresholds required for autonomous clinical deployment; restricted strictly to non-contrast chest CT volumes, excluding contrast scans, other body parts, and other 3D modalities such as MRI or PET.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Self-supervised pretraining (CT-CLIP), supervised multi-abnormality classification, volume-to-volume retrieval, text-to-volume retrieval, multimodal visual question answering (CT-CHAT), and automated radiology report generation. Split into 20,000 patients for training and 1,304 patients for internal validation. Not approved for routine clinical deployment.
